$comment: The gallery, as data. `tag` is the capability the exhibit is the proof of, and `prompt` is the one sentence that would ask for the world above it — ordinary user voice, no jargon, because the gallery is the page's argument that a sentence is enough. Every `caption` is the exhibit's OWN panel subtitle, verbatim, and every `fact` is a number the exhibit itself measured and printed — file and line in `factFrom`. `by` is the vendor whose agent built that exhibit from `docs/GALLERY.md` alone, and it is the only thing the tile mark says; a row with no `by` was built inside this repository with a person in the loop, and the /built section is where that distinction is stated rather than implied. Adding an exhibit is a row here and nothing else. `docs/GALLERY.md` specifies eighteen exhibits and one hero; all nineteen are built, and `pending` is empty rather than deleted so the build still has a shape to print if the list ever grows again.

hero.name: Lamp Road
hero.caption: A valley at dusk, and the proof that the seams fit.
hero.prompt: a valley at dusk with a road up to a shrine, and pilgrims who will not walk into the dark

live.name: Crowd
live.prompt: a busy piazza with hundreds of people crossing it, all walking somewhere
live.caption: Nine hundred walkers, one expression, no per-walker state.
live.idea: A walker's position is pathSample(route, ((phi*i + t*v) mod 1) * arcLength). There is no walker struct.

live.name: Island
live.prompt: a small island where I can watch a whole day go by in a minute
live.caption: One day, in ninety seconds.
live.idea: Terrain, a shoreline, trees, and a full day/night cycle — the palette lerp doing the whole job.

live.name: Clay
live.prompt: a valley where I can push the ground up with my cursor and everything on it resettles
live.caption: The ground is material. Drag it, and watch everything else resettle.
live.idea: Raise a ridge and the water re-routes, the walkers re-plan, and the trees ride it up and slide off.
live.fact: 2,200 props over a live height field

live.name: Harbor
live.prompt: a harbor at dusk with tall masts and cranes, and a long jetty out over the water
live.caption: Tall thin objects, one depth order.
live.idea: A mast is a twentieth of a tile wide and twelve storeys high, and only its base says where it belongs. One DepthSorter holds every hull, crane and the ninety-two-tile jetty.

live.name: Wayfinding
live.prompt: a crowded hall where I can close a gate and watch everyone find another way round
live.caption: One field, six hundred and forty readers, one rebuild.
live.idea: There is no per-walker path. Closing a crossing rebuilds one field, and every walker's next read returns a different answer — so a map change costs the same whatever the crowd is.

live.name: Builder
live.prompt: a yard where I drop a workshop down and it tells me when it will not fit
live.caption: Footprints, a ghost, validity, and the tap-to-tile seam.
live.idea: One predicate between the pixel a finger landed on and the six tiles it would occupy. The ghost, the color under it and the refusal are all that same boolean.

live.name: Caverns
live.prompt: a cave lit only by scattered lanterns, with the pools of light overlapping
live.caption: Pools that meet without a seam.
live.idea: The light field costs its buffer, not its light count — which is why the price is flat from 104 pools to 704.

live.name: Orbit
live.prompt: stations turning in space with stars behind them and no ground anywhere
live.caption: No ground at all — platforms, stars, a cold palette.
live.idea: No TileGrid, no terrain pass and no height field. Every platform's angle is a closed-form function of t, and three star bands carry the depth the ground usually would.

live.name: Replay
live.prompt: a marsh I can record, wind back, and prove came out the same
live.caption: Tap the marsh to seed a bloom. Then scrub the tape: every frame is recomputed from the seed and the log, never remembered.
live.idea: The bar re-runs from tick zero on every pointer move, checks each checkpoint as it passes, and can come back red — a check that cannot fail proves nothing.

live.name: Terraces
live.prompt: stepped terraces on a hillside where I can click on any level and hit the one I meant
live.caption: Elevation, and why a tap needs the terrain.
live.idea: On ground with height the obvious screen-to-tile conversion is wrong, and it is wrong by more the higher you climb.
live.fact: the naive pick misses by 1,400 px at the ridge

live.name: Instrument
live.prompt: a hall of pipes I can play, where I can see the sound being made
live.caption: Sound with no files.
live.idea: The ribbon in the air is Audio.onScheduled — what the synthesizer was asked to make, drawn before it is audible. An analyser would draw the speaker instead.

live.name: Endless
live.prompt: a world I can keep panning across forever that never loads anything
live.caption: Pan forever. Nothing is loaded and nothing is kept.
live.idea: Chunks are minted from the seed as you reach them and evicted behind you. Come back and they are identical.

live.name: Canyon
live.prompt: a desert canyon cut by a river, with a slider that rewinds a million years
live.caption: A million years of a river. The bar re-runs the model.
live.idea: Erosion accumulates, so the scrub bar is a deterministic re-run from the nearest checkpoint, never a lookup.

live.name: Idle
live.prompt: a little brick works that keeps earning while I am away
live.caption: Fourteen hours, one step.
live.idea: The price of the next kiln is b·r^k evaluated rather than accumulated, so buy-max is arithmetic; a fourteen-hour absence is one advanceOver between two frames.

live.name: City block
live.prompt: a city block at night from above, with traffic in the streets and lit windows
live.caption: Setback massing and a window rhythm. Every value here is in the URL.
live.idea: The technique that carries the whole look: one color per solid, three faces derived, a rhythm of warm windows.

live.name: Migration
live.prompt: an old save file opened by five newer versions of the same game
live.caption: A v1 save opened by a v5 build, one rung at a time.
live.idea: Four migrations declared once, and five sealed builds fall out of the same chain. A crate that a build refuses topples back over the rung it failed, named.

live.name: Resonance
live.prompt: a puzzle in a ruin where every gate hums a chord and I answer it by ear
live.caption: Answer the chord.
live.idea: A puzzle you solve by ear. Every gate hums a chord; you carry six tuned strings and no audio files exist.
live.fact: 6 ms attack on a struck string

live.name: Errand
live.prompt: a small village game where I walk around, talk to people, take things and save
live.caption: Walk, talk, take, use, save. The whole genre, small enough to read.
live.idea: Five verbs and deliberately no sixth. The save envelope is about sixty bytes and the HUD prints its size.

$order: Heavy and light alternate down the grid on purpose. Two columns means two tiles run at once, and Crowd (900 walkers) beside Clay (10,247 draw calls over a live height field) was measured at a 23.3 ms worst gap where the same pair split across rows is 20.2 ms. The gallery running budget is a layout decision, not only a code one. The eight agent-built rows are interleaved rather than appended for the same reason, and for one more: eight of them in a block at the foot of the grid would be a second gallery, and they are not — they are exhibits, held to the same standard, standing beside the others.
